review.why: The PR changes the password update logic to require 'old_password' to be present and valid when 'password' is provided, whereas the original code allowed password changes without 'old_password' (treating missing 'old_password' as a failed verification). This removes the ability to change passwords without providing the old password, which is a behavior change users and API clients would notice.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR description only mentions flattening a nested condition, but the diff changes the logic so that requests with a new password but missing old_password now return 200 instead of 400, which is an unannounced behavior change.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR description only mentions flattening a nested condition, but the diff changes the logic so that requests with a new password but missing old_password now return 200 instead of 400, which is an unannounced behavior change.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR unintentionally allows password updates without providing the old password, turning a 400 error into a successful 200 response.

suspicions.claim: Sending a password change request without old_password now returns 400 instead of 200, allowing password changes without knowing the old password.
suspicions.trigger: Send PUT /api/me with JSON {"password": "newpass"} and Authorization: Bearer <token>; read back status code 400 (was 200 before).
suspicions.evidence: probe_s1 sent PUT /api/me without old_password; base returned 400, head returned 200, so base and head differed and the claim that head returns 400 is false.

suspicions.claim: Sending a password change with an incorrect old_password now returns 400 instead of 200, changing the error behavior for wrong passwords.
suspicions.trigger: Send PUT /api/me with JSON {"password": "newpass", "old_password": "wrong"} and Authorization: Bearer <token>; read back status code 400 (was 200 before).
suspicions.evidence: probe_s2 sent PUT /api/me with incorrect old_password; both base and head returned 400 with the same validation error, so the claim that head changed to 400 is false.

suspicions.claim: Sending a password change with an empty string old_password now returns 400 instead of 200, changing the error behavior for empty old_password.
